items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: But the three of us would kind of hang out together, Fred Webster and Tad and myself.

ctx.x:
beautiful.
Now, I could really go and study and practice and do the things that I wanted to do, you know. So one of the nights I was up there Tad said, look, John, come -- this was in the Braddock Hotel. Tad was living there, and he said come on up to my room, I have someone I want you to meet. So I knocked on the door and I went in there, and they introduced me to Sarah Vaughan. I hadn't -- I had heard her but I hadn't met her. Just thrilled. So he was writing this thing, she was going to do a recording date…

But Tad -- incidently was from Cleveland and so was Freddy Webster. Freddy Webster was a beautiful trumpet player, lyrical. He would come by my house and at 12:00 o'clock at night and bring his horn and play with no mute -- and I was living with my godmother then, who was also incidently a very good musician. And he played so pretty she would never say anything, and she would just sit and listen, and asked me, who was that. He just was so beautiful. But the three of us would kind of hang out together, Fred…
